text: Which one of the following compounds is non-aromatic?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Molecules are aromatic if they are

(1) Cyclic

(2) Planar

(3) Conjugated

(4) Molecules who have (4n + 2) $π$ electrons [This is called Huckel's Rule]

Aromatic compounds are highly stable.

(a) 
[IMG]


(1) Molecule is cyclic.

(2) All atoms which are completing the cyclic ring have $sp^{2}$ hybridisation. So its shape is planar. If any one atom is $sp^{3}$ hybridised then molecule shape will be non planar.

(3) It is conjugated means all $π$ bonds are showing resonance with each other.

So all atoms which are forming cyclic ring are participating in resonance. That is called conjugated.

(b) 
[IMG]


(1) This compound is cyclic

(2) All atoms are $sp^{2}$ hybridised. So molecule shape is planar.

(3) It is conjugated as all $π$ bonds are showing resonance.

(4) It has 6$πe^{-}$. So obey Huckel Rule.

$\therefore$ Compound is aromatic.

(c) 
[IMG]


(1) This compound is cyclic

(2) All atoms are $sp^{2}$ hybridised. So molecule shape is planar.

(3) It is conjugated as $π$ bond is showing resonance.

(4) It has 2$πe^{-}$. So obey Huckel Rule.

$\therefore$ Compound is aromatic.

Anti-Aromatic :-

It is highly unstable.

Anti-aromatic compounds are -

(1) Cyclic

(2) All atoms which is forming cyclic ring are planar.

(3) it is conjugated.

(4) It has 4n$πe^{-}$.

Here no anti-aromatic compounds presents.

Non-Aromatic :-

Those compounds which are not either aromatic or anti-aromatic.

Definition : All cyclic compounds which are comparatively stable with its open chain analogous system, compound is known as non aromatic compound.

(a) 
[IMG]


Here one carbon is $sp^{3}$ hybridised that is why it's structure is non planar. So this cyclic compound will be neither aromatic nor anti-aromatic. It will be non aromatic.

Multiple cyclic rings :-

To find nature of this ring, make maximum possible $π$ bonds in the outer ring. This is a hypothetical structure. Here outer ring should be largest conjugated ring means outer ring should have these $π$ bonds which are in resonance with each other.

And the nature of the outer ring will be same as the original molecule.

(d)
[IMG]


From this structure we can't decide the nature as all $π$ bonds are not present in the outer ring that is why we make right resonating structure where all $π$ bonds present in the outer ring.

Outer ring :


[IMG]


As outer ring is aromatic so original compound will also be aromatic.

Note :-

Even though from left resonating structure we can't decide the nature of the molecule, it does not mean it's nature is not aromatic. As different resonating structures don't have different nature. All resonating structure have same nature.

text:
According to Bohr's atomic theory :

(A) Kinetic energy of electron is $\propto \frac{Z^{2}}{n^{2}}$.

(B) The product of velocity (v) of electron and principal quantum number (n), ${}^{'}vn^{'}\propto Z^{2}$.

(C) Frequency of revolution of electron in an orbit is $\propto \frac{Z^{3}}{n^{3}}$.

(D) Coulombic force of attraction on the electron is $\propto \frac{Z^{3}}{n^{4}}$.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In Bohr's model for a hydrogen-like species of atomic number $Z$, $r_{n}\propto \dfrac{n^{2}}{Z}$ and $v_{n}\propto \dfrac{Z}{n}$.

(A) $\text{KE}=\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}\propto \dfrac{Z^{2}}{n^{2}}$, so (A) is correct.

(B) $v\times n\propto \dfrac{Z}{n}\times n=Z$, not $Z^{2}$, so (B) is incorrect.

(C) Frequency of revolution:

$f=\dfrac{v}{2πr}\propto \dfrac{Z/n}{n^{2}/Z}=\dfrac{Z^{2}}{n^{3}}$

so (C) is incorrect.

(D) The nucleus carries charge $Ze$, so the Coulombic force on the electron is

$F=\dfrac{1}{4πε_{0}}\dfrac{(Ze)(e)}{r^{2}}\propto \dfrac{Z}{r^{2}}\propto Z\times \dfrac{Z^{2}}{n^{4}}=\dfrac{Z^{3}}{n^{4}}$

so (D) is correct.

Only (A) and (D) are correct.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift

text: Which one of the following carbonyl compounds cannot be prepared by addition of water on an alkyne in the presence of HgSO$_{4}$ and $H_{2}SO_{4}$?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Hydration of an alkyne with $\mathrm{HgSO}{}_{4}$/dil. $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$ follows Markovnikov's rule: OH adds to the more substituted carbon, and the enol formed tautomerises to a carbonyl compound.

Only ethyne gives an aldehyde, so (D) can be prepared:

$\mathrm{HC}\equiv \mathrm{CH}{}_{\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}\qquad }^{\mathrm{HgSO}{}_{4}}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{OH}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CHO}$

A terminal alkyne $\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{C}\equiv \mathrm{CH}$ gives the methyl ketone $\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$: but-1-yne (or but-2-yne) gives butan-2-one (A), and ethynylcyclohexane gives cyclohexyl methyl ketone (B).

Propanal, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CHO}$, would need OH on the terminal carbon of propyne, but Markovnikov addition puts it on C-2, so propyne gives acetone, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}$. Propanal cannot be obtained this way.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift

text: The correct set from the following in which both pairs are in correct order of melting point is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Correct option is (D), i.e. LiF > LiCl; MgO > NaCl. Melting point is directly proportional to lattice energy. Lattice energy is the energy required to separate a mole of an ionic solid into gaseous ions. It depends upon charge of ions and size of ions.

$M.P.\propto L.E.\propto \frac{Charge}{Size}$

$\begin{array}{ll} Li\to +1 & Li\to +1 \\ F=-1 & Cl\to -1 \end{array}$

Both LiF and LiCl having same charge, so melting point will depend on size.

Larger the size of anion, lesser the lattice energy and hence, melting point order is LiF > LiCl.

Similarly, $\begin{array}{ll} MgO & NaCl \\ Mg\to 2+ & Na\to 1+ \\ O\to 2- & Cl\to 1- \end{array}$

MgO having + 2 charge which is greater than NaCl (+ 1) charge. So, greater the charge on the ions greater will be lattice energy and hence, melting point order is MgO > NaCl.

text: The calculated magnetic moments (spin only value) for species $[FeCl_{4}]^{2-}$, $[Co(C_{2}O_{4})_{3}]^{3-}$ and $MnO_{4}^{2-}$ respectively are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $[\mathrm{FeCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$, $x+4(-1)=-2$ gives $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$, $3d^{6}$. The complex is tetrahedral and $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ is a weak-field ligand, so $\Delta _{t}$ is small and no pairing occurs: $e^{3}t_{2}^{3}$, with $n=4$.

$μ=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{4\times 6}=\sqrt{24}=4.90\text{BM}$

In $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}){}_{3}]{}^{3-}$, $x+3(-2)=-3$ gives $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$, $3d^{6}$. Oxalate is a weaker ligand than water, but the high charge of $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ makes $\Delta _{o}>P$ (as with $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ and $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$), so the complex is low spin: $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$, with $n=0$ and $μ=0$.

In $\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}$, $x+4(-2)=-2$ gives $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{6+}$, $3d^{1}$, with $n=1$.

$μ=\sqrt{1\times 3}=\sqrt{3}=1.73\text{BM}$

The values are 4.90, 0 and 1.73 BM.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift

text: The formula of a gaseous hydrocarbon which requires 6 times of its own volume of $O_{2}$ for complete oxidation and produces 4 times its own volume of $CO_{2}$ is $C_{x}H_{y}$. The value of y is $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Combustion reaction :

$C_{x}H_{y}(g)+\left (x+\frac{y}{4}\right )O_{2}(g)\to xCO_{2}(g)+\frac{y}{2}H_{2}O(l)$

Suppose, volume of $C_{x}H_{y}$ is V and volume of $O_{2}$ is 6 times greater than $C_{x}H_{y} = 6V$

then volume of xCO$_{2}$ $\Rightarrow$ $V_{x} = 4 V$

x = 4

Since, $V_{O_{2}}=6\times V_{C_{x}H_{y}}$

$V\left (x+\frac{y}{4}\right )$ = 6V

$\left (x+\frac{y}{4}\right )=6$ ..... (i)

Put value of x = 4 in Eq. (i) we get,

$4+\frac{y}{4}=6\Rightarrow y=8$

text: The solubility product of PbI$_{2}$ is 8.0 $\times$ $10^{-9}$. The solubility of lead iodide in 0.1 molar solution of lead nitrate is x $\times$ $10^{-6}$ mol/L. The value of x is $__________. ($Rounded off to the nearest integer) [Given $\sqrt{2}$ = 1.41]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{Pb}(\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}){}_{2}$ is a strong electrolyte, so the solution already has $[\mathrm{Pb}{}^{2+}]=0.1$ M.

Let the solubility of $\mathrm{PbI}{}_{2}$ in it be $S$ mol L${}^{-1}$:

$\mathrm{PbI}{}_{2}\qquad (\mathrm{s})\mathrm{Pb}{}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq})+2\mathrm{I}{}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})$

Then $[\mathrm{I}{}^{-}]=2S$ and $[\mathrm{Pb}{}^{2+}]=0.1+S\approx 0.1$ M, since $S\ll 0.1$.

$K_{sp}=[\mathrm{Pb}{}^{2+}][\mathrm{I}{}^{-}]^{2}=0.1\times (2S)^{2}=8.0\times 10^{-9}$

$4S^{2}=8.0\times 10^{-8}\Rightarrow S^{2}=2\times 10^{-8}\Rightarrow S=\sqrt{2}\times 10^{-4}=1.41\times 10^{-4}=141\times 10^{-6}\text{mol L}^{-1}$

Hence, the answer is 141.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift

text:
Assuming ideal behaviour, the magnitude of log K for the following reaction at 25${}^{\circ }$C is x $\times$ $10^{-1}$. The value of x is $______________. ($Integer answer)

$3HC\equiv CH_{(g)}⇌C_{6}H_{6(l)}$

[Given : $\Delta _{f}G^{o}(HC\equiv CH)=-2.04\times 10^{5}$ J mol$^{-1}$ ; $\Delta _{f}G^{o}(C_{6}H_{6})=-1.24\times 10^{5}$ J mol$^{-1}$ ; $R = 8.314 J K^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Reaction,

$3HC\equiv CH(g)_{Acetylene}\to C_{6}H_{6}(l)_{Benzene}$

Given, $\Delta G_{f}^{o}(CH\equiv CH)=-2.04\times 10^{5}$ J mol$^{-1}$

$\Delta G_{f}^{o}(C_{6}H_{6})=-1.24\times 10^{5}$ J mol$^{-1}$

Gibb's free energy, $\Delta G_{f}^{o}=-nRT\ln K$

$\Delta G_{f}^{o}=\sum (\Delta G_{F}^{o})_{P}-\sum (\Delta G_{F}^{o})_{R}$

$-nRT\ln K=-n^{'}RT\ln K_{p}-(-n^{''}RT\ln K_{f})$

$\Rightarrow -RT\ln K=1\times (-1.24\times 10^{5})-(-3\times 2.04\times 10^{5})$

$\Rightarrow$ $-2.303\times R\times T\log K=4.88\times 10^{5}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\log K=-\frac{4.88\times 10^{5}}{2.303\times 8.314\times 298}$

$\Rightarrow$ $n\ln K=n^{'}\ln K_{p}-(-n^{''}lnK_{f})$

$\Rightarrow$ |log K| = 85.52 

$\Rightarrow$ |log K| = 855 $\times$ $10^{-1}$

x = 855

text: $C_{6}H_{6}$ freezes at 5.5${}^{\circ }$C. The temperature at which a solution of 10g of $C_{4}H_{10}$ in 200g of $C_{6}H_{6}$ freeze is $__________$ ${}^{\circ }$C. (The molal freezing point depression constant of $C_{6}H_{6}$ is 5.12${}^{\circ }$C/m.)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Pure solvent : $C_{6}H_{6}(l)$

Given, 

$T_{f}^{o}=5.5^{\circ }C$

$K_{f}=5.12^{\circ }C/m\Rightarrow m=200g$

$m_{solute}=10g$

Molar mass of solute $C_{4}H_{10}=12\times 4+10=58$

Solute $(C_{4}H_{10})$ is non-dissociative;

$\therefore$ i = 1

$\therefore$ $\Delta T_{f}=iK_{f}m$

$\Rightarrow (T_{f}^{o}-T_{f}^{1})=1\times 5.12\times \frac{(10/58)}{(200/1000)}$

$5.5-T_{f}^{1}=\frac{5.12\times 5\times 10}{58}\Rightarrow T_{f}^{1}=1.086^{\circ }C$

or $T_{f}^{1}\approx 1^{\circ }C$

text:
Sucrose hydrolyses in acid solution into glucose and fructose following first order rate law with a half-life of 3.33 h at 25${}^{\circ }$C. After 9 h, the fraction of sucrose remaining is f. The value of $\log _{10}\left (\frac{1}{f}\right )$ is $________$ $\times$ $10^{-2}. ($Rounded off to the nearest integer)

[Assume : ln 10 = 2.303, ln 2 = 0.693]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}_{Sucrose}+H_{2}O⟶^{1storder}C_{6}H_{12}O_{6}_{Glu\cos e}+C_{6}H_{12}O_{6}_{Fructose}$

$t_{1/2}=\frac{10}{3}h$

At t = 0, a = [A]$_{0}$      (initial conc.)

t = 9h, a $-$ x = [A]$_{t}$         [conc. at time t]

For using 1st order equation,

$K=\frac{2.303}{t}\log \frac{[A]_{0}}{[A]_{t}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{K\times t}{2.303}=\log \frac{[A]_{0}}{[A]_{t}}$

$\frac{\ln 2\times 9}{10/3\times 2.303}=\log \left (\frac{1}{F}\right )\Rightarrow \log \left (\frac{1}{F}\right )=0.8124$ ($\because$ $k=\frac{\ln 2}{t_{1/2}}$)

$\log \left (\frac{1}{F}\right )=81.24\times 10^{-2}$

x = 81.24 or x $\approx$ 81

text:
The total number of amines among the following which can be synthesized by Gabriel synthesis is $__________$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used to prepare $1^{o}$ aliphatic or alicyclic amine. Hence, amine which can be synthesised by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis method contains $α$-carbon.

Aniline $(C_{6}H_{5}NH_{2})$ does not contain $α$-C cannot be prepared by Gabriel reaction.

Remaining amines all contain $α$-C in its respective position, hence they can easily give Gabriel phthalimide reaction.
